name: MonarchDialog
title: Dialog
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.BasicAlertDialog (window, scrim, focus, back and Escape, motion) with a Monarch panel; androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog for a full-screen form
summary: A modal dialog: MonarchDialog is the Material 3 BasicAlertDialog with a Monarch panel (title, description, content and actions on the raised surface). The platform keeps the window, scrim, focus and back.
whenToUse: When the person must read or decide something before going on: an AlertDialog with a title, a message and up to two buttons, or a Dialog with Monarch components for a short form. For a form that fills a phone, a full-screen Dialog with a top app bar.
whenNotToUse: Not for information that can wait: use a MonarchBanner or a snackbar. Not for a long task with several steps on a phone: use ModalBottomSheet (see sheet) or a screen of its own. Not for a choice of actions: use DropdownMenu.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, dismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = dismissible, paneTitle: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called on back, Escape or a tap on the scrim, unless not dismissible. Stop showing the dialog here.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading at 18/600, also the pane title TalkBack reads when the dialog opens.

options.name: description
options.description: A short line under the title, 14 in the muted text colour.

options.name: dismissible
options.description: Whether back, Escape and a tap on the scrim dismiss it. False while work runs or when a choice is required.

options.name: actions
options.description: The buttons at the end, right aligned, for example a ghost Cancel and a primary MonarchButton. They wrap when there is no room.

options.name: content
options.description: The body under the description; it scrolls when the dialog is taller than the window.

states.name: shown
states.description: The dialog is centered over the scrim and takes focus; the screen behind does not respond.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: Back, a tap on the scrim or a button calls onDismissRequest; the app stops composing the dialog.

states.name: busy
states.description: With dismissOnBackPress and dismissOnClickOutside set to false while an action runs, and a loading MonarchButton, the dialog stays until the action ends.

states.name: full screen
states.description: With usePlatformDefaultWidth = false the Dialog fills the window, for a form on a phone.

appearance: A panel up to 512dp wide and 16dp from the window edges, 16dp corners, the raised background with a subtle border (strong in the high-contrast themes), one soft shadow in the light themes and none in the dark ones, 20dp padding, the title at 18/600 and the description at 14 in the muted text role. Actions are MonarchButtons, right aligned with 8dp between them. The scrim dims by the alpha of the overlay scrim role.
platformNotes: The web Dialog is one component with sizes, a header, a footer, a close button with closeLabel, busy, closeOnOutsideClick, escapeGuard and fullScreenOnPhone. On Android: the header is title and description, the footer is actions, closeOnOutsideClick is dismissOnClickOutside, busy and escapeGuard are dismissible = false, and fullScreenOnPhone is a Dialog with usePlatformDefaultWidth = false, a Scaffold and a TopAppBar. A dialog stays until the app stops composing it, so unlike the iOS alert it can show progress and errors itself. There is no close button by default; a Cancel action or the back gesture closes it. Content with its own heading (a celebration) passes title = null and a paneTitle for TalkBack.
accessibility: The dialog is a separate window: focus and TalkBack move into it, stay there, and return to the screen when it closes.
TalkBack reads the title as the pane title and as a heading.
Back and Escape call onDismissRequest unless dismissible is false.
The action buttons keep 48dp targets; name them after the action ("Delete project"), not "OK".
The title and description wrap at font scale 2.0; the content scrolls.
edgeCases: A long message scrolls inside AlertDialog's text slot at the largest font size.
With dismissOnClickOutside = false a tap on the scrim does nothing; keep a visible way to close.
On a phone in landscape a tall Dialog is cut by the window; make its content scroll.
